findings.finding: Conflicting assumption between siblings about whether the inbound absence-probe emit path is reachable in production. J11 (5200) row-14 requires asserting an '(inbound, probe)' entry in the dry-run plan and its REQUIRED SEQUENCING note points at differ.py:630-650 as the emitter, treating that path as reachable once a binding exists. Sibling d103-c3f8-2fbc-4c97 establishes the opposite: differ.compute_mutations's sole production caller (run_differs.py:222) passes the previous JIRA snapshot into the local_state parameter, so the absent-partner probe loop (_compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes, differ.py:610-650) 'is unreachable — which also makes the entire (inbound, probe) dispatch chain a documented subsystem with no live producer.'
findings.location: child 5200-e04e-246e-4aae (row-14 absence-probe AC) vs child d103-c3f8-2fbc-4c97
scenarios: The J11 row-14 cell arranges a binding then a delete then a dry-run and asserts a probe entry appears; if the probe emitter is in fact inert at the production call site (as d103 states), the cell either cannot pass, or passes via a different code path than the AC's cited emitter — either way the two children disagree about the mechanism.
findings.suggested_fix: Have 5200 cite the actual production emitter for the deletion probe (or the differ path fixed/relied upon), and cross-reference d103 so the row-14 sequencing note does not depend on a differ arm d103 documents as inert.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Deconflict 5f48 and b4e3: make one child own the DC identity-mint fix (apply_inbound_records.py) and mark the other as depending-on / duplicating it, rather than both carrying independent RED-first ACs for the same observable.
evidence: 5f48 AC set: 'an inbound apply under the DC backend mints a ghost identity successfully, asserted by a test that FAILS on today's code'; 'the identity is minted under the shared jira provider/channel'; 'a test asserts the failure is not merely swallowed — i.e. the mint is observed to SUCCEED'; 'CREATION_CHANNELS is UNCHANGED'.

b4e3 AC set duplicates these: 'an inbound apply under the DC backend MINTS a ghost identity for a DC-shaped assignee (one with name and NO accountId), asserted by a test that FAILS against today's code'; 'that identity is minted under the SHARED jira provider/creation channel'; 'the test asserts the mint SUCCEEDED — not merely that no exception escaped'; 'CREATION_CHANNELS is UNCHANGED'.
b4e3's Scope explicitly claims apply_inbound_records.py and folds in 5f48: '(Folded in from bug [rebar:5f48-244c-7063-42d0]...)'.
findings.finding: Scope overlap: the DC inbound identity-mint fix is fully specified as acceptance criteria on TWO sibling children with the same observable outcome. Bug 5f48-244c-7063-42d0 ('DC inbound identity mint fails silently') and J7 b4e3-1de0-3188-40a1 both carry near-identical ACs for the same deliverable: an inbound apply under the DC backend mints a ghost identity under the shared 'jira' provider/channel, asserted by a test that FAILS on today's code and proves the mint SUCCEEDED (not merely no-exception), with CREATION_CHANNELS unchanged.
findings.location: child 5f48-244c-7063-42d0 (and its overlap with child b4e3-1de0-3188-40a1)
scenarios: Two children owning one code change (the identity path in apply_inbound_records.py) is a double-ownership hazard: if worked independently, the second would find the first already landed and its RED-first ACs unsatisfiable, or two conflicting edits to the same call site.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a depends_on (or duplicates) link from 5f48 to b4e3 and scope 5f48's ACs to what b4e3 does not deliver, or explicitly note in 5f48 that its fix rides b4e3's change so its ACs are verified there.
